turn_text: Brad, do you think there's a disconnect in Washington between what farmers and agriculture does and the people that are there?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I think everyone loves to eat, right? But no one No one really pays much attention out there to how the food is put on their plate and appreciate where it comes from. And quite frankly, the challenge is it takes to provide that to our country and the world. So there is a misunderstanding for just current practices. I look at farmers in southern Minnesota and just from an environmental standpoint how how innovative and how just amazing we've been with adapting and improving our technology and our practices. It rarely gets noticed by folks in Washington. We also are faced with challenges that I think are unique to the industry, unique to the country in regards to the workforce issues, shortage of workforce, the supply chain issues and, and quite frankly, the lack of leadership on the world stage, which has put us in a very vulnerable position from an input side. So when we look at, for instance, Urea and other fertilizer inputs, when we're seeing 200 to 400% increases in those inputs, that affects our bottom line.
